newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cardenas won Mexico City mayor debate - polls.
newsitem.headline: Cardenas won Mexico City mayor debate - polls.

text.p: Left-winger Cuauhtemoc Cardenas won a televised debate Sunday night against ruling party rival Alfredo del Mazo in the campaign for mayor of Mexico City, according to three opinion polls.
The debate was the only direct confrontation so far in the campaign for the July 6 election. No others have been planned.
Radio reports said Monday that just under half the voters in Mexico City watched the debate, broadcast on several radio and television stations simultaneously.
Indemerc/Louis Harris told Reuters their telephone sample of just over 400 people showed 49.8 percent declaring Cardenas and his Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) the winner.
The survey showed that 26.3 percent thought neither candidate had won and 23.9 percent thought Del Mazo and his Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) had won.

Mori de Mexico, in a survey published in La Jornada newspaper, said 43 percent gave Cardenas as the winner, against 21 percent for Del Mazo. Another pollster, CEO, awarded Cardenas 40.2 percent against 19.5 percent for Del Mazo, La Jornada said.

Cardenas decided to exclude his main conservative rival, Carlos Castillo Peraza, from the debate because Castillo had attacked him for handing a public beach property to his mother while Cardenas was governor of the state of Michoacan in the 1980s.
Cardenas currently leads most polls to win the mayor's race by a comfortable margin. Castillo is second placed, but tending to lose ground to Del Mazo, who is third.
